snippets.snippet_text: "Etsy advertises that it takes around 3.5% commission on sales, which is of course very low. Unfortunately, that is simply not true. If you tot up all the additional fees the actual figure is closer to 15%. And that's before you've paid for postage, any marketing fees and local taxes."

"paying for off-site ads and to appear higher in listings are both necessary to be successful on Etsy. I did pay for marketing for a year as an experiment, and I found that although I made more sales, they basically covered my marketing budget."

"in 2025 when the USA increased their import tariffs I was effectively no longer able to sell to the USA either since customers aren't likely to buy if the postage and taxes cost more than the item itself."

possible_subjects: Etsy: stated commission ~3.5% vs. effective total fees ~15% when all platform fees included; before postage, marketing, and local taxes
Etsy: paid off-site ads and promoted listings described as necessary for success; year of marketing cost roughly equalled additional sales revenue
Etsy seller (international): US tariff increases in 2025 effectively ended ability to sell to US buyers due to prohibitive postage and tax costs
